_about: Clinic heal game `foot` (D15i, decision 27; js/clinic/heal/games/foot.js). The sole of the foot, toes up. The soak (which water: paani [hot]/[cold]/[lukewarm], how many jugs), then each splinter dragged out along its lighter channel with square turns to the edge of the foot: touching the side is an 'ow', it slides back to the last turn and loses the steady-hand row (a scored skill row, no words); then a plaster on each spot. Level 1 one straight channel; level 2 two channels with one or two turns; level 3 three channels from three toes, three turns each and narrower, the toes named for the order (pela [big toe], ne poi ...). Sides only in the diagnosis (D10). The channels, splinters and widths are in the code (PATHS, halfW per level); the levels, rows and words below the game's code are the older design's notes, kept for reference.

sore-feet.english: sore feet from dancing all night at the wedding (and a thorn from the garden)

paani.english: paani (the jug: hot or cold is chosen in the game)

loon.english: loon (the salt pot and its spoon)

1._note: The bath (hot or cold paani) + two toe calls by size (either foot) + the thorn in the sore foot (it shows a swirl), named by size + the plaster. Lines one at a time.

2._note: + the salt count (hakro/ba/trae chamcho loon); three toe calls. Said as one list.

3._note: + the side, in the patient's voice, on every toe (size x side: one toe of ten); no swirl shows which foot.

camera._about: D2 (1 Oct): the sole is seen from the front-on wide shot (the art plan §2.1).
camera._target: A1 (5 Oct): the match cut. target = where the close-up draws the sore part and size = its radius, in the close-up's 800 x 500 units: the push-in ends with the patient's part (from the art's anchor) at that place and size.

art._about: The art plan's P1 (closeups/<set>/sole.webp, child and adult sets), swapped in by file name when it exists; the channels and splinters stay code.

place._about: A1 (5 Oct): P1 placed so its big toe (360, 195 in the 1024 x 1536 source) and little toe (750, 397) land on the mirrored stand-in's (298, 70) and (508, 78): the sole's width and length match the stand-in's outline, so the channels and their clip still fit. The art's toes slope down to the little toe where the stand-in's are level, so level 3 (channels from the toes, toes named) keeps the stand-in until the toes are re-placed. Mirrored in code when the big toe is on the right.
